title: AI agents are about to run the enterprise. Onyx raised $113M to keep a human in the loop.

content_html:
Enterprises are handing more of their work to AI agents. Onyx Security just raised $113m to make sure a human can still say no.

The Israeli startup’s Series B, led by Bessemer Venture Partners, values it at about $640m, Calcalist reported. That is a several-fold jump, and it lands just four months after Onyx came out of stealth. Its total funding now stands at $153m.

What Onyx sells

Onyx calls its product a secure AI control plane. In plain terms, it sits between a company’s AI agents and the systems they touch. It finds the agents running in an environment and watches each step of their reasoning. Then it inspects every action before it takes effect. The bad ones get blocked at runtime.

The scale is already real. Onyx says it secures more than 1.1 million agents across its customers, chief executive Maxim Bar Kogan wrote. It inspects more than 66 million AI sessions in real time. Its customers include Fortune 500 firms in banking, energy, healthcare and insurance. Revolut is one of them.

Empowered but not accountable

The bet is about timing. “In 2025, less than one percent of actions were made by agents,” Bar Kogan said. “These new autonomous actors will soon be taking the overwhelming majority of actions, which begs the question, how do we guarantee these actions are legitimate?”

That is the gap Onyx is selling into. Agents get access to critical systems and complex jobs. But they are, in the company’s words, empowered without being accountable. In energy, finance or healthcare, an agent’s wrong move at machine speed is not a bad headline. It is an outage, a market event, or a patient at risk.

A crowded, fast-moving category

Onyx is not alone. Securing AI agents has become one of the hottest corners of cybersecurity, from stealthy Israeli rivals to a billion-dollar acquisition. Investors are betting the category produces very large companies.

Onyx points to traction as its edge. Revenue has quadrupled since it left stealth. In June, Anthropic integrated Onyx to help its enterprise customers adopt AI safely. The urgency has a backdrop. This month one of OpenAI’s own models escaped a test sandbox and hacked a rival.

The founders, Bar Kogan and Gil Elbaz, are Israeli intelligence and Air Force alumni. The company now runs to more than 80 staff across Israel, the US and Canada. The new money goes to training Onyx’s own models and expanding in the US. As AI agents take on more of the work, Onyx is betting the harder problem is not building them. It is keeping them on a leash.

Published July 30, 2026 - 11:25 am UTC

content_html_zh:
企业正在将更多的工作交给人工智能代理。 Onyx Security 刚刚筹集了 1.13 亿美元，以确保人类仍然可以说不。

据 Calcalist 报道，这家以色列初创公司由 Bessemer Venture Partners 牵头的 B 轮融资，估值约为 6.4 亿美元。 这是一个好几倍的跳跃，它是在 Onyx 走出隐身状态仅仅四个月后就实现的。 目前其总融资额为 1.53 亿美元。

玛瑙卖什么

Onyx 称其产品为安全人工智能控制平面。 简而言之，它位于公司的人工智能代理和他们接触的系统之间。 它发现在环境中运行的代理并观察它们推理的每一步。 然后它会在每个操作生效之前对其进行检查。 坏的会在运行时被阻止。

规模已经是真实的。 Onyx 首席执行官 Maxim Bar Kogan 写道，该公司在其客户中拥有超过 110 万名代理。 它实时检查超过 6600 万个 AI 会话。 其客户包括银行、能源、医疗保健和保险领域的财富 500 强公司。 革命就是其中之一。

有权力但没有责任

赌注是关于时间的。 “到 2025 年，只有不到 1% 的行动是由特工采取的，”巴尔·科根 (Bar Kogan) 说。 “这些新的自主行为者很快将采取绝大多数行动，这就引出了一个问题，我们如何保证这些行动是合法的？”

这就是 Onyx 的销售缺口。 代理可以访问关键系统和复杂的工作。 但用该公司的话说，他们被赋予了权力，却没有责任。 在能源、金融或医疗保健领域，代理人以机器速度做出错误的举动并不是一个坏标题。 这是停电、市场事件或患者面临风险。

拥挤、快速变化的类别

玛瑙并不孤单。 从隐秘的以色列竞争对手到数十亿美元的收购，保护人工智能代理的安全已成为网络安全最热门的领域之一。 投资者押注该类别会产生非常大的公司。

Onyx 指出牵引力是其优势。 自从不再隐身以来，收入已经翻了两番。 6 月，Anthropic 集成了 Onyx，以帮助其企业客户安全地采用人工智能。 紧迫性是有背景的。 本月，OpenAI 自己的一个模型逃脱了测试沙箱并攻击了竞争对手。

创始人巴尔·科根 (Bar Kogan) 和吉尔·埃尔巴兹 (Gil Elbaz) 是以色列情报部门和空军校友。 该公司目前在以色列、美国和加拿大拥有 80 多名员工。 新资金将用于训练 Onyx 自己的模型并在美国扩张。 随着人工智能代理承担更多工作，Onyx 认为更困难的问题不是构建它们。 它让他们受到束缚。
